To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the majority of multidrug-resistant isolats of the Acinetobacter calcoacticus-Acinetobacte baumannii complex were positive for adeABC and adeI, and that these two genes were associated with the int1 gene.

The majority of clinical isolates of the Acinetobacter spp. complex were multidrug-resistant and belonged to A. baumanii, and the presence of adeSR/adeABC/adeE/adeIJK/Int1 genes was associated with high-level multidrug resistance.
the majority of multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter isolates are positive for the adeSR-ade ABC and adeIJK efflux system genes, whereas adeE expression is not detectable.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the distribution of multidrug efflux system genes in clinical isolates and the relationship between the efflux system and the presence of the integron genes.
the identification of the molecular basis of multidrug resistance and the possible use of RND genes as indicators for different Acinetobacter spp. in a clinical context.
the molecular epidemiology of multidrug resistance in clinical Acinetobacter isolates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
adeABC, adeIJK and adeDE are not associated with multidrug resistance in A. baumannni, but adeABC and adeI/JK are associated with multidrug-resistance in Acinetobacter sp.
the adeABC and adeI/J genes are present in A. baumanniii and the adeDE gene is present in Acinetobacter spp. other than A. baumanniiii.
the adeABC/adeDE/adeIJK genes are associated with multidrug resistance in Acinetobacter spp.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
multidrug resistance in Acinetobacter spp. is likely due to the combined effects of the expression of the adeABC and adeI JK efflux pumps and class 1 integrases.

adeSR-adeIJK is a good marker for the presence of multidrug-resistant A. baumannni (i.e. A. baumannnii 2) and the absence of these markers is a good indicator of A. calcoaceticu (i.e. Acinetobacter 3).

adeABC and adeI JK are the major multidrug efflux systems in A. baumannni and that the presence of these genes is associated with multidrug resistance in A. baumanii, while in A. calcoaceticu s, adeE is a more important efflux system for resistance to aminoglycoside and beta-lactams.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of adeABC/adeDE/adeIJK in multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter isolates is likely associated with the presence of class 1 integrons.
the presence of adeABC and adeI in the Acinetobacter spp. genome is associated with the development of multidrug resistance.
the presence of adeSR/adeABC, adeIJK, adeDE and class 1 integrase genes in clinical isolates of the Acinetobacter genus is associated with multidrug resistance.
